architecture_direction.status: Research only; no proven stable chunk identity, complete invalidation contract or game implementation.
constraints: Game draw-state bytes mutate before cloning; pointer identity alone is not a valid cache key.
Moving only the measured DXMT encoder is limited to 6.61% aggregate baseline CPU before overhead; this is not an FPS ceiling.
Existing translated shaders require preserved instance IDs and argument bindings. GPU completion must precede reuse of frame-slot constants/resources.
Exact byte recurrence can establish potential eligibility only; it cannot prove mesh/resource lifetime or replay safety.

binding_records.status: Do not integrate padding or unconditional interning on this evidence.
limitations: Source-owned synthetic records, not actual game binding distributions or consumers.
Combined time adds producer wall time and delayed full-byte consumer time; this is not aggregate CPU or FPS.
First pass was potentially contaminated by a concurrent correctness rebuild and excluded.
Interning pays hashing and full equality; a proven unchanged-state version could avoid both, but no such contract has been established.

constructor_recycling.status: Do not build or install a fused Wine adapter on this evidence.
limitations: Host allocation backend, not the Wine heap.
Original constructor extracted only from the locally owned hash-verified game into ignored build files. No game code is exported.
Initial callback-inlining-biased measurements excluded; corrected pass preserves Win64 calls and virtual dispatch.
The TLS comparison uses a private 10-byte byte-swap callback cheaper than the real indexed GS/TLS path; its raw values should not be compared directly with the preceding fixture.
Native C++ exception/termination semantics would need to be preserved before any game adapter.
The added memory retention and integration surface are not justified by a robust substantial parallel gain.

native_batch_tuned_comparison.scope: Synthetic retained AABBs, one semaphore request/reply per batch. Input extraction/marshalling, scene updates and GPU work excluded. The game's culling cost and eligible batch sizes are unmeasured. This is not game performance evidence.
native_batch_tuned_comparison.interpretation: The AVX2 target did not improve this Rosetta kernel; native large-batch feasibility remains, but the best original x86 baseline should be used when reporting savings. Target flags alone are not a demonstrated optimization.
